summary: The CRADA statute. A federal lab may contribute people, facilities, equipment and intellectual property but not money; the partner may contribute money and the same kinds of resources. (b)(3)(A): the lab may accept, retain and use funds, personnel, services and property from a collaborating party.
The collaborating party is offered the option of an exclusive license for a pre-negotiated field of use for inventions made under the agreement.
The Government retains a nonexclusive, paid-up license.
(c)(4): special consideration to small business firms and consortia involving small business firms; preference for U.S.-located businesses agreeing to manufacture substantially in the United States.
(c)(5): the agency has 30 days to disapprove or require modification of an agreement.
(c)(7)(A): a partner's trade secrets and privileged or confidential commercial information are not disclosed.
(c)(7)(B): information produced under the agreement may be protected for up to 5 years; agencies may authorize a total of not more than 30 years.
